expected_behavior: No ongoing clipboard polling or reads occur; any transient in-memory original strings are wiped immediately.
what_remains_useful: Zero CPU overhead and zero risk of unintended text collection when capture is toggled off.
notes: Validates explicit opt-in privacy invariant: DevGuard never monitors the clipboard without explicit local consent.

expected_behavior: Change count match triggers immediate deduplication; no repeated Gemma or Gitleaks inference invocation for duplicate text within same scope.
what_remains_useful: Preserves inference queue budget and local battery/CPU while keeping text accessible.
notes: Protects against repetitive polling loops on active clipboards.

scenario_name: Copy A then B before A finishes (Rapid Copy Overwrite)
expected_behavior: Gemma evaluation of version 10 is invalidated/canceled; only current version 11 sets the final state. Version 10 cannot overwrite the clipboard or publish obsolete findings.
what_remains_useful: Benign shell command in version 11 is immediately ready without stale sensitive warnings.
notes: Prevents race conditions in clipboard event processing.

expected_behavior: Cleaned text replaces clipboard contents; internal hash marker prevents a recursive self-scan loop on the synthetic redaction marker.
what_remains_useful: Developer can paste cleaned database connection string directly into assistant chat without leaking production credentials.
notes: Demonstrates the core user workflow: detect, sanitize, and supply safe text to clipboard with operator confirmation.

scenario_name: Large text, image or unsupported host
expected_behavior: Explicitly labelled SKIPPED or UNSUPPORTED; never falsely marked as 'CLEAR/SAFE'. Oversize or binary payloads are ignored without memory explosion.
what_remains_useful: Clear audit log notice indicating payload exceeded capture budget or was non-text.
notes: Honest limitation enforcement: does not attempt image OCR or universal clipboard scraping.

action: User pastes uncleaned clipboard into Slack or TextEdit prior to DevGuard evaluation
expected_behavior: DevGuard explicitly states it cannot block OS-wide arbitrary pastes before analysis completes. Managed gates (Codex hooks, DevGuard API) protect destination channels.
what_remains_useful: Accurate security posture; does not claim miraculous OS-kernel-level universal paste interception.
notes: Crucial requirement from AGENTS.md and COVERAGE.md: do not overclaim universal interception.
